newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities flat in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt volatilities flat in thin trade.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were little changed in extremely thin pre-Christmas trade, dealer said.
With the underlying markets also steady, there was little inclination to take fresh option positions ahead of a holiday and the year-end, they said.
"It's a wasted day," said a Treasury bond option trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Trading at the CBOT and Chicago Mercantile Exchange was to finish early on Tuesday and will be closed all day on Wednesday.
Implied volatilities for CBOT February and March T-bond futures options stood at about 9.0 and 9.7 percent, a touch below Monday's closings.
Implied volatilities for CME March and June Eurodollar futures options were steady at around 8.8 and 13.7 percent.

Earlier in the day, the market showed little reaction to a 1.3 percent rise in chain-store sales in the week ended December 21 from the prior week in the BTM/Schroders weekly survey. Sales for the week rose 4.8 percent year-on-year. The numbers were largely in line with market expectations.
A Eurodollar trader for a U.S. bank affiliate at the CME said the market briefly looked nervous but soon regained calm.
Although sizable option deals were scarce, a Japanese house was said to have sold 1,000 contracts of June 94.25 puts and bought short-June 93.25 and 93.50 puts.
Short-June contracts are options whose expiration is in June 1996 but whose prices are based on June 1997 futures. They have higher gamma values than plain-vanilla June options.
One trader said such a spread was a cheap way to buy short-June options with less concern about the steeper time decay inherent in the high-gamma contracts.

Options generally become more vulnerable to time decay as their expiration date approaches. For front-month Eurodollar options this pattern is reinforced by a tendency of underlying futures to gravitate toward parity levels against cash Eurodeposit rates if there is little scope for a change in interest rates.

If the Federal Reserve shows no sign of shifting its monetary policy, June option volatilities would ebb early, while short-June options with similar delta value at this point would retain their value longer.
